title: Adaptive Preflight Eval Orchestrator with Tenant Budgets & Backpressure
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement an orchestrator that triggers adaptive preflight evals when a model version is pinned or upgraded (catalog and tenant-pinned). Unlike prior proposals that fan out uniform checks, this ticket designs a tenant-aware fanout that considers per-tenant sampling budgets, traffic shape, and real-time system load (backpressure) to avoid overloading serving capacity and overspending eval budget. The orchestrator should ensure high-risk pins are evaluated more comprehensively while respecting tenant quotas and global budget windows.
technical_design: High-level components: 1) Trigger listener: subscribes to pin/upgrade events from catalog and tenant API; 2) Risk profiler: computes an initial risk score per event using heuristics (change magnitude, model family, config diffs, customer SLAs, previous regression history); 3) Sampling planner: produces a per-tenant eval plan (sample size, synthetic vs live shadowing, priority) constrained by tenant budget, global eval budget, and current serving load; 4) Dispatch layer: schedules executions across worker pool with rate limiting and adaptive parallelism; 5) Early-stop controller: monitors partial eval signals to cancel or scale down remaining work; 6) Result aggregator and scorer: computes differential metrics and flags regressions to the catalog/console. Implementation notes: use existing eval-runner infra (ENG-42177) as a library; add a lightweight scheduler service (k8s deployment) with Redis for ephemeral plan state; expose PromQL metrics; persist plans and outcomes to the audit store for compliance and postmortems.
acceptance_criteria: 1) On a model pin event, the orchestrator starts a tenant-scoped eval plan within 30s for >95% of events; 2) The orchestrator respects tenant budget caps (no plan exceeds tenant budget) for 100% of sampled tests in QA trials; 3) Under synthetic load, the orchestrator backs off when serving latency SLO (99p latency) approaches threshold, verified via stress tests; 4) Regression detection precision >= 90% on labeled regression dataset and false positive rate < 5%; 5) All plans produce a causal summary artifact and store it in the catalog audit log; 6) Dashboard shows per-event cost estimate and actual spend with <5% variance over runs.
rollout_plan: Phased rollout: 1) Internal dev env - unit + integration tests (week 1); 2) Canary within infra team for low-volume catalog pins (week 2): run orchestrator in 'report-only' mode that does not cancel runtime traffic, only writes alerts; 3) Tenant opt-in Beta: enable for selected customers with explicit budget controls and allow toggling; 4) Global opt-in with conservative default budgets and automatic backpressure enabled; 5) Post-rollout: run two-week observation window before enabling auto-block/rollback policies. Each phase gated by SRE signoff and cost telemetry checks.
test_plan: Automated: unit tests for planner heuristics; integration tests for end-to-end flow using mocked serving runtime and eval-runner; chaos tests that simulate spikes in serving latency and ensure backpressure triggers. Manual: run sample pin events for three tenant tiers (trial, standard, enterprise) with curated prompts and known regressions to validate detection. Load test: synthetic fanout to emulate 1k concurrent tenant pins within a 10m window to validate rate limiting and early-stop behavior.
monitoring_and_metrics: Expose metrics: eval_plans_started, eval_plans_completed, eval_plan_cancelled, eval_cost_estimate, eval_cost_actual, eval_detected_regressions, eval_false_positives, eval_latency_slo_backoffs. Create dashboards: per-tenant spend and success rate, system-level backpressure heatmap. Alerting: page on >5% of plans cancelled due to runtime overload or when cost variance >25% for a tenant in 24h.
notes: Trade-offs considered: 1) Heavy fanout increases detection coverage but raises cost and risk to runtime — mitigated via tenant budgets and adaptive backpressure; 2) Conservative sampling for low-tier tenants to control spend; 3) Using Redis for plan state provides low-latency but requires careful TTL and cleanup to avoid orphaned plans. Open question: should shadow traffic evaluation be counted against tenant budgets or absorbed by platform credit? Recommended: count shadow eval compute against an 'eval' budget separate from production compute and surface a chargeback model.
comments: 2026-02-15 Maya Chen: Initial draft and acceptance criteria posted. Assigned to Diego for implementation. Linked initial spec in Confluence.

2026-02-22 Diego Alvarez: Spike complete — implemented a prototype scheduler that uses token-bucket per-tenant. Prototype repo at https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-orch-spike. Observed that large enterprise tenants with long prompt lists need batching heuristics to avoid long-running plans.

2026-02-26 Priya Nair (SRE): Reviewed backpressure approach. Suggested integrating latency signals from runtime-prometheus exporter and using a soft threshold at 80% of SLO before aggressive throttling. Also requested a canary that uses 'report-only' mode first.
2026-03-03 Diego Alvarez: Implemented early-stop controller and added PromQL metrics (eval_latency_backoff_count). Added integration test harness. Creating PR next week to evaluation repo.

2026-03-10 Erin Park (Product): Confirmed customer-facing UX needs: per-pin cost estimate displayed in the Console approval flow and ability for enterprises to opt for more exhaustive checks. Linked to PM ticket PM-92277 for UI integration.

2026-03-11 Diego Alvarez: Started canary in infra namespace in 'report-only' mode. First 48h results: 128 pin events processed, 3 flagged potential regressions, average per-plan cost 14% below estimate due to early-stop savings. No SLO violations recorded. Moving to tenant-beta after signoff.
